Shipping the Reader

Last month we finally shipped the reader pipeline. The hardest part was not parsing at all: it was deciding what not to parse.

Every parser grows until it contains an ad-hoc, informally-specified implementation of half a browser.

Three lessons stood out:

  • Ship the smallest format first and lock its behavior with golden tests
  • Make every lossy decision visible as a diagnostic
  • Keep provenance in original-source coordinates

The full write-up of the plumbing is in the design notes.
